chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajistani told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Mu'az told us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn al-Mub al-Mubarak, saying: Sho'bah ibn al-Hajjaj told us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The son of Adam perishes, or he said: grows old, but two things remain in him: greed and aspiration.

key_terms.ابْنُ آدَمَ: Son of Adam, referring to humanity
key_terms.الْأَمَلُ: Aspiration, hope, or expectation (often of longevity or success)
key_terms.الْحِرْصُ: Greed or eager desire for worldly gain

ai.seo_question: What two things remain young in humans as they age according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the psychological paradox of human aging, where physical decay contrasts with the persistence of insatiable desire (al-hirṣ) and endless hope (al-amal). In Shia scholarly tradition, this serves as a cautionary reminder that despite the inevitability of death, the soul remains trapped in worldly attachment until it achieves spiritual maturity or faces its reckoning.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-113 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sejezy narrated that Muhammad ibn Mu’az quoted Al-Hussein ibn al-Hassan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mobarak, on the authority of Sho’abat ibn al-Haj’jaj, on the authority of Abi Qatadah, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
The Children of Adam (people) will get old or die, but two things still remain young in them: greed and aspirations.”
